cs.t: This is a really good card that keeps on getting better. After my steam deck battery puffed up and my RX580 became too old to play any modern games, I had two choices: 1. Upgrade to a new GPU - this was costing me $300 at the very least for a 3 year old card 2. Hope to get a steam machine - but the crazy queue and the $1000 price tag really soured me on this 3. Get a bc-250 for $150 and make do for a year or two before upgrading. I'm so glad I went with this option. I just used my old atx power supply and old PC case. Everything almost just works. It consumes lot less power than my previous gaming PC. It's a lot more silent. Some times there's a crash or two. I'm waiting to upgrade the power connector before unlocking it's full potential (40 compute units, and the two extra cores). So far I've finished playing Spider-Man 2, Hogwarts legacy, now playing 007 first light.
cs.th: ASRock BC-250: Building the Budget Steam Machine

cs.t: I was tasked with getting 20,000 PS5 APU's online. ASRock BC-250. Each chassis had 12 independent blades and in order to save money, we decided to not put SSD/NVMe into them and iPXE boot them instead. Each APU had 16GB of memory, but the only issue was that it wasn't ECC, so they would randomly fail. It took a lot of effort but it actually worked!
cs.th: Sandia turns on brain-like storage-free supercomputer

cs.t: Support for the board is also way better than before. Now you can customize RAM assigned to cpu/gpu, idle power, in some cases unlock cores, distros work out of the box, etc. And the alternative of getting a gpu, cpu, ram, storage is like 5 times as expensive.
